native.audio.backend.btWasapiExclusive: WASAPI exclusive · Bluetooth (lossy codec to headset)
native.audio.backend.btWasapiShared: WASAPI shared · Bluetooth (lossy codec + OS resample)
native.audio.backend.btCpalShared: cpal shared · Bluetooth (lossy codec to headset)
native.audio.backend.cpalTight: cpal shared (tight buffer) · OS mixer still resampling
native.audio.rgDesc: Normalises perceived loudness across the catalog by applying the gain encoded in each file's {tags} tags. Track mode varies song-to-song and is best for shuffle; album mode preserves intentional loudness differences within an album and is best for sequential listening.
native.audio.rgNextTrack: Settings apply on the next track — the currently-playing track stays at its original level until it ends or you skip.
native.audio.rgImmediate: Changes apply immediately. Files without tags play at their native level, and the gain is capped at each file's peak so it never clips.
native.audio.rgOffHint: Play at native level — no normalisation
native.audio.preampDesc: Adjusts the overall ReplayGain output by a fixed dB offset. ReplayGain's reference is conservative; +6 dB is a common boost for catalogs mastered hot enough that the default attenuation feels quiet. Clamped to ±15 dB — peak limiting still applies, so positive boosts won't clip.
native.audio.browserHint: These settings apply to music played in this browser. The native audio engine, exclusive output and bit-perfect options live in the OnScreen desktop app.
native.audio.engineDesc: When on, music playback routes through the OS-native audio engine (cpal + claxon, with the WASAPI / CoreAudio / ALSA exclusive-mode paths layered on top) instead of the browser's {element} element. The audiophile-pillar settings below — ReplayGain, exclusive output — only apply on this path; with the native engine off they're inert. Switch takes effect on the next track.
native.audio.engineToggle: Use the native audio engine for music playback
native.audio.exclusiveDesc: Tightens the audio buffer so the OS mixer's resampler runs at lower latency. {bitPerfect} (no mixer resampling at all) needs platform-specific work — Windows WASAPI exclusive mode, macOS CoreAudio HOG mode, or Linux ALSA {hw} direct — and isn't on by default yet. This switch is the on-ramp: when those backends ship per platform, your existing choice carries over. New tracks pick up the change; the currently-playing track keeps its current config until it ends.
native.audio.tightBuffer: Tight-buffer mode (~10 ms at file native rate)
native.audio.btOverride: Treat output as Bluetooth (lossy codec, not bit-perfect)
native.audio.btOverrideHint: Auto-detection only catches devices Windows reports through the Bluetooth bus driver — wireless brands like Soundcore, Sony, and Bose look identical to wired headphones in Windows' device properties. Flip this on if your output is a Bluetooth headset and the badge above doesn't already say so.
native.audio.btWarning: Output is a {device}. Bluetooth audio always inserts a lossy codec (SBC, AAC, aptX, or LDAC) between OnScreen and your headset — bit-perfect playback is not achievable on this output regardless of WASAPI mode. The Windows system volume is also applied digitally before the BT encoder, so volume changes will modify samples. For the audiophile path, switch to a wired DAC or USB headset.
native.audio.resampleWarning: The OS audio engine is resampling this {rate} kHz / {bits}-bit file down to your device's mix-format before it reaches the DAC. Decoded samples are lossless, but the playback chain is not bit-perfect. {enable} to send the file at its native rate.
native.audio.sharedHint: Shared mode lets the OS mix OnScreen with other apps, but it inserts a sample-rate converter between us and your DAC. For bit-perfect output enable exclusive mode above.
native.audioTest.desktopOnly: This diagnostic page only works inside the OnScreen desktop client.
native.audioTest.title: Native audio engine — diagnostic
native.audioTest.intro: Lists every output device the desktop client's {backend} backend can see, and plays a brief sine-wave test tone on demand. Use this to verify the audio path works on your hardware before the engine takes over playback.
native.audioTest.noDevices: No output devices reported by cpal.
native.audioTest.flacIntro: Streams a FLAC file from any URL through the engine end-to-end — HTTP fetch → claxon decode → cpal at the file's native rate. Use {path} against your server to test with real library content; supply the bearer token from {storage} after a successful login.
native.server.title: Server connection
native.server.intro: The OnScreen server this desktop app connects to. Saved on this device only — not synced to the server.
native.server.desktopOnly: This page is only meaningful inside the OnScreen desktop client.
native.server.switchHint: To switch servers, enter the new address — for example {example1} or {example2}. It's tested before anything changes. Switching to another server signs you out of this one.
native.server.engineDesc: When enabled, FLAC playback bypasses the browser's {element} element and goes through the Rust cpal+claxon pipeline — the bit-perfect path. Other formats (MP3, AAC, transcoded sources) still fall back to {element}; if a non-FLAC URL hits the engine it'll fail to decode and the AudioPlayer logs the error and skips the track.
native.server.engineLimits: Phase 1 limitations (will close in subsequent commits): position counter doesn't update during native playback; track doesn't auto-advance at end (use the Next button).
native.server.engineToggle: Use the native audio engine for FLAC playback
native.server.disconnectHint: Signs out, forgets this server and returns to the first-run setup screen.
native.server.confirmForgetThis: Sign out and forget this server?
